title: Who deserves the winnings
source_checks: Relevant full passages checked in published economics papers, the December 2015 Rothschild–Scheuer author version, Nakamura Nobel lecture, Nichia company statement, DARPA institutional records, and previously checked MusicLab, Merton, Kickstarter and Google sources. Named version/access boundaries are retained. This is a chapter claim check, not independent proof certification or a completed whole-book review.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 70 and 72–75 (PDF pp. 2 and 4–7), especially pp. 73–74 reactor purchase, failed growths, repeated modifications and two-flow design
claims: Inventor recounts unsuccessful GaN growths and 1.5 years of reactor modifications
Credits Akasaki and Amano advances
Blue light plus phosphor can yield white light
sources.boundary: Retrospective inventor account with technical citations, attributed accordingly; not independent allocation of all causal credit, no fabricated laboratory observation and no asserted social-value percentage. Device measurements are additional evidence beyond allocation records.

sources.locator: Opening three substantive paragraphs and company positions 2–4; full relevant indexed primary text read
claims: Announced remuneration JPY608570000 and interest damages JPY235340000, total JPY843910000
Scope includes many patents, pending applications, foreign counterparts and unpublished know-how from Nakamura employment
Company emphasized employer risk and defended its position
sources.boundary: Company press statement is an interested party account. No claim that it independently establishes a causal contribution percentage; no district-court award account, current legal guidance or inferred reaction from Nakamura. Rounded main-text figures identified as approximate.

claims: March 13, 2004 million-dollar prize unclaimed because no finalist finished
October 8, 2005 five finishers on 132-mile course; Stanford Stanley winner, 6h53m, two-million-dollar prize
sources.boundary: Organizer account; the two courses differ. No estimated causal effect of doubling the prize or attributed long-run autonomy impact. Race observations include more than identity of prize recipient; no budget estimate.

sources.boundary: Comparison conditions on funded ventures at one anonymous firm; not a test on all rejected ideas, investor skill in general or proof success is pure luck. Birch financing illustrations are original hypothetical applications.

narrative_checks: Lockdown opens a new question about rewards, rather than retelling the entire experiment.
Nakamura lecture and Nichia settlement supply different documented objects; no invented biography, dialogue, reaction or visit.
DARPA defined prize performance carries prospective-incentive argument; failure and further testing remain distinct.
Four explanations for fictional executive pay separate production, avoidance, bargaining and reinforced historical position.
Kerr, Piketty–Saez–Stantcheva and Rothschild–Scheuer receive substantive credit with full relevant versioned source passages.
Merton and van de Rijt retain earlier credit and add recognition and initial-support questions.
Contribution, contractual entitlement, incentives and moral desert remain distinct; author proposed values are explicit.
No equal-merit conclusion, luck percentage, optimal tax rate, actual-firm lifetime diagnosis or dismissal of physical evidence.
6000 main words; headings and notes excluded; transition to Chapter 7 physical AI inputs.
whole_book_review: Still required: final continuity, repetition, pace, conceptual/factual/citation review, author review of normative voice, complete bibliography and combined word budget.
